title: Scalar projection mates and coherence for field geometric sections
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Work on sites small in compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ for profinite $P$, and $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. For a commutative condensed ring $R$ put $R_T=p_T^*R$, use internal module categories and ordinary unbounded derived categories, and write $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for internal $R$-modules with $\underline G$-action [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $a:X\to s$ be the structure morphism of a qcqs $k$-scheme, $X^s=X\times_k k^s$ with projection $u$, and $\varphi:R\to R'$ any condensed ring map. Suppose given field data $E_R,E_{R'}$, their normalized scalar adjunction data, and the ordinary and derived geometric section identifications of [def-sfb-field-action-transport-data, def-sfb-field-action-scalar-transport-data, def-sfb-field-action-geometric-transport-data]. Use $\mathcal K_R$ as in [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent] and assume the geometric and scheme scalar-restriction comparisons $\rho$ are the canonical derived composition comparisons with identity ordinary section maps. For every $M\in D(R_X)$ put $S_T=R'_T\otimes^L_{R_T}-$, $S_G=R'\otimes_R^L-$ and let $\eta$ be the scalar unit. Define
$$\beta_M:S_G\mathcal K_R(M)\longrightarrow\mathcal K_{R'}(S_XM)$$
to be the scalar-adjunction transpose of $\mathcal K_R(M)\xrightarrow{\mathcal K_R(\eta_M)}\mathcal K_R(\operatorname{Res}_X S_XM)\xrightarrow{\rho}\operatorname{Res}_G\mathcal K_{R'}(S_XM)$.

Then the corresponding field-side transpose $\chi_M:S_sRa_{*,R}M\to Ra_{*,R'}S_XM$ is exactly the coefficient projection whose adjunct under $a_{R'}^*\dashv Ra_{*,R'}$ is
$$a_{R'}^*S_sRa_{*,R}M\cong S_Xa_R^*Ra_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{S_X\varepsilon_M}S_XM.$$
The direct-image comparison $\rho$ is conjugate to the derived pullback comparison $a_{R'}^*S_s\cong S_Xa_R^*$; the conjugacy counit equation and the two adjunction triangle identities identify the scalar transpose with this displayed adjunct even when $\varphi$ is non-flat. Under $D(E_{R'})Ra_{*,R'}\cong\mathcal K_{R'}$ and the normalized scalar-extension comparison, $D(E_{R'})(\chi_M)=\beta_M$.

After restricting to the slices at $\bar s$ and $X^s$ and using $p_{X^s}=p_{\bar s}a_s$, the forgotten $\beta_M$ is precisely
$$R'\otimes_R^LRp_{X^s*}u^*M\longrightarrow Rp_{X^s*}(R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}u^*M).$$
Its adjunct under the $R'$-linear point adjunction is scalar extension of the point counit after the canonical pullback/scalar-tensor exchange. Its $R$-linear form is the projection mate for $p_{X^s}$ with tensor argument $R'$. These are the same morphism under scalar adjunction, using the conjugacy equation for the coefficient/geometric square. Thus the object identifications and the projections give coefficient data of [def-sfb-field-action-coefficient-transport-data].

All these object comparisons and specified morphisms are natural in input morphisms, compatible with scalar restriction, and commute with canonical integer shifts. The coefficient-restriction squares use the cocycle of the normalized direct-image composition, and the shift structures are the canonical right-derived and adjoint unit/counit-compatible ones. In particular the projection commutes with shifts in $M$, not just in its scalar tensor argument. Exactness of geometric coefficient pullbacks and of the separably closed field presentation suffices for the composition-adjunction normalization; scalar extension itself is not assumed exact.

proof.text: Write $L=a_R^*$, $F=Ra_{*,R}$, $L'=a_{R'}^*$, $F'=Ra_{*,R'}$, and $V_T=\operatorname{Res}_T$. All products denote functional composition. By [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization] the specified internal scalar/pullback comparison is the natural isomorphism $\lambda:L'S_s\cong S_XL$, normalized on K-flat tensors and on the actual geometric adjunctions. It requires no flatness. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], the coefficient square also has an adjunction-compatible comparison $b:LV_s\cong V_XL'$ (the inverse of that lemma's $b$). Its right comparison is the given $\rho:F V_X\cong V_sF'$, with the inverse orientation to that lemma's $d$. The hypotheses hold because $a^{-1}R_s\cong R_X$ and $a^{-1}R'_s\cong R'_X$ are the cartesian coefficients pulled from the point, and their ring-map square commutes. That lemma is stated for the adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] with $u=a$ and $c$ the coefficient identifications from the point, while the internal normalization lands in the ringed derived pullback and K-injective direct image of the section model [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization]. These coincide: the section-model inverse image is the same tensor-formula pullback $a^{-1}(-)\otimes_{a^{-1}R_s,c}R_X$ with the same ordinary module adjunction, exact because $c$ is invertible, so its derived functor is termwise on every complex, and both direct images are computed on K-injective resolutions. Hence both derived adjunctions are the unique bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] induced by that one ordinary adjunction, over $R$ and over $R'$. Thus these are the canonical composition comparisons, rather than a new choice of isomorphisms.

proof.text:
The comparison $\rho$ is conjugate to $\lambda$ for the composite adjunctions $L'S_s\dashv V_sF'$ and $S_XL\dashv FV_X$: apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] to the two routes from $(X,R'_X)$ to $(s,R_s)$, one changing coefficients at $X$, the other at $s$. Identity-underlying-topos coefficient morphisms have left derived functors $S_T$ and exact right adjoints $V_T$. Its conjugacy counit equation applies with no exactness assumption on $S_T$. The same comparison's geometric-restriction form, or directly step 1's transpose equation, gives, for every $N\in D(R'_X)$,
$$V_X(\varepsilon'_N)\,b_{F'N}\,L(\rho_N)=\varepsilon_{V_XN}.$$
Let $\eta^T$ be the scalar units. Scalar-adjunction normalization of the pullback exchange says
$$V_X(\lambda_A^{-1})\,\eta^X_{LA}=b_{S_sA}\,L(\eta^s_A).$$
Indeed the inverse scalar mate of $b$ is $\lambda^{-1}$: on flat-term K-flat representatives both send the inverse image of $m\otimes r'$ to the same balanced tensor, with unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. These two equations specify the directions of all comparisons used below.

source.place: Tags 0D6D, 0D6E, 07A6; agent application of conjugacy to the coefficient square and its normalized scalar mate

proof.text:
Set $A=FM$, $N=S_XM$, and let $\chi:S_sA\to F'N$ be the scalar transpose of $\rho_NF(\eta^X_M)$. Its geometric adjunct is $t=\varepsilon'_N L'(\chi)$. Compute the scalar transpose of $t\lambda_A^{-1}:S_XLA\to N$, using step 2 and naturality of $b$:
$$\begin{aligned}
V_X(t\lambda_A^{-1})\eta^X_{LA}
&=V_X(\varepsilon'_N)b_{F'N}L\bigl(V_s(\chi)\eta^s_A\bigr)\\
&=V_X(\varepsilon'_N)b_{F'N}L(\rho_N)LF(\eta^X_M)\\
&=\varepsilon_{V_XN}LF(\eta^X_M)
=\eta^X_M\varepsilon_M.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is naturality of the geometric counit. The scalar transpose of $S_X(\varepsilon_M)$ is also $\eta^X_M\varepsilon_M$, by naturality of the scalar unit. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore gives $t=S_X(\varepsilon_M)\lambda_{FM}$, exactly the displayed adjunct of the item. The unit/counit transpose formulas are [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; their inverse property is the two triangle identities. Thus this calculation compares the actual arrows, without assuming any scalar extension is exact.

Transport the scalar transpose defining $\chi$ through $D(E_R)$ and $D(E_{R'})$. The scalar squares in [def-sfb-field-action-scalar-transport-data] preserve every Hom transpose, including its units. The geometric identifications of [def-sfb-field-action-geometric-transport-data] are normalized by the identity ordinary section maps and the total-derived units. The scheme and geometric restriction comparisons in the hypothesis have the same normalization. Their square therefore commutes: its two routes are the direct-image composition comparisons for the same ringed composite, with the identity ordinary section map, and the cocycle [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] equates these routes. Consequently the transported untransposed arrow is exactly $\mathcal K_R(\eta_M)$ followed by the stipulated geometric $\rho$. Since its scalar transpose is the definition of $\beta_M$, we get $D(E_{R'})(\chi_M)=\beta_M$ under the specified object and scalar-extension identifications.

proof.text: Put $v:\bar s\to s$, $a_s:X^s\to\bar s$. Use [lem-sfb-field-free-orbit-derived-slice-sections]: the slice at $h_{\bar s}$ is forgetting the action, and $v^*FM\cong Ra_{s*}u^*M$ uses precisely the given section normalization. Its final clause preserves the actual geometric counit and K-flat scalar comparison. More explicitly, [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison], with $f=a$ and target sheaf $h_{\bar s}$, gives source sheaf $a^{-1}h_{\bar s}=h_{X^s}$ and the equation $u^*(\varepsilon_M)\theta_{FM}=\varepsilon^{a_s}_{u^*M}a_s^*(\beta^{\rm slice}_M)$. Apply this to the adjunct computed in step 3; K-flat scalar exchange restricts to the exchange for the restricted rings. Thus its restriction is exactly the scalar extension of the $a_s$-counit, preceded by the restricted pullback/scalar comparison. This uses arbitrary sheaf slices, so does not assume $\bar s\to s$ is an object of an affine small-site presentation.

source.place: Modules on Sites Tag 04IF (lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi); normalized unbounded slice counit equation

proof.text:
Identify the pro-etale topos of $\bar s$ with the condensed topos, as in the stipulated field presentation, and use $p_{X^s}=p_{\bar s}a_s$. The left adjoints $a_s^*$ and the coefficient pullback $p_{\bar s}^*$ are exact; the latter is an equivalence. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] to this composite, separately over $R$ and $R'$. Its normalized counit is the composite counit
$$\varepsilon^p_H=\varepsilon^{a_s}_H\circ a_s^*(\varepsilon^{p_{\bar s}}_{Ra_{s*}H}),\qquad H=u^*M.$$
The normalized scalar square for $p_{\bar s}$ is part of the given scalar data [def-sfb-field-action-scalar-transport-data]. Paste this square with step 5's restricted square. Expanding the two geometric adjuncts gives $S_{X^s}(\varepsilon^{a_s}_H)\circ S_{X^s}a_s^*(\varepsilon^{p_{\bar s}}_{Ra_{s*}H})$ after their pullback/scalar exchanges. Naturality of those exchanges moves the second counit through them; the displayed composite is $S_{X^s}(\varepsilon^p_H)$. The adjunction bijection then identifies the forgotten $\beta_M$ with
$$R'\otimes_R^LRp_{X^s*}H\longrightarrow Rp_{X^s*}(R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}H),$$
whose $R'$-linear point adjunct is the prescribed scalar extension of $\varepsilon^p_H$. This is equality in the derived category, not only after cohomology.

source.place: Derived Categories Tag 09T5 (lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); Tag 0D6E, exact-left-adjoint composition and its composite counit

proof.text:
For the $R$-linear form at $p=p_{X^s}$, use [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] on both the condensed site and $X^s_{\rm proet}$ to identify internal and ring-sheaf scalar adjunctions. No flatness is needed. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] to the two coefficient/geometric routes over $p$; its conjugacy equation changes the $R'$-linear point adjunct of step 6 to the $R$-linear adjunct
$$p_R^*(R'\otimes_R^LRp_*H)\cong R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}p_R^*Rp_*H\xrightarrow{1\otimes\varepsilon^p_H}R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}H.$$
To see this is the specified exchange, [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] sends $p^{-1}(r'\otimes m)$ to $p^{-1}r'\otimes p^{-1}m$, with the same scalar unit. This is exactly the symmetric version of the projection mate for tensor argument $R'$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Hence the two linear forms agree under scalar adjunction, with the given conjugacy normalization.

proof.text: All displayed constructions use natural transformations and adjunction bijections natural in both variables, so substitution of $M\to N$ gives the required input squares. For coefficient restriction, regard each restriction as direct image on an identity-underlying-topos ring morphism. The two routes through a successive restriction and a geometric direct image are the two parenthesizations of one triple composite; [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] equates them. Pasting with the normalized scalar squares preserves their Hom transposes. Thus the coefficient-restriction squares commute for $\chi$ and $\beta$, and also after the slice/point identifications of steps 5–7. For successive extension maps the specified projections obey the cocycle of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]; its identity and commutative-coefficient-square clauses ensure that these are the canonical coefficient comparisons, with no invertibility of projection assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, normalized composition cocycle; Tag 0E47 (remark-compose-base-change-horizontal), coefficient projection cocycle

proof.text: For shifts, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] gives the canonical unit/counit-compatible shifts on the geometric adjunctions, and also on each scalar adjunction viewed as the derived adjunction of an identity-underlying-topos coefficient morphism. The given scalar and geometric data preserve these shifts. The K-flat tensor/pullback exchanges have the canonical signed total-tensor shift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Therefore shifting the defining adjunct $S_X(\varepsilon_M)\lambda_{FM}$ gives exactly its counterpart at $M[n]$; the shift-compatible adjunction bijection gives the same equation for $\chi$. Step 4 transfers it to $\beta$; steps 5–7 transfer it to the point projection. In its $R$-linear form the required first-input shift equation is stated explicitly by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift], applied to $p_{X^s}$ with fixed tensor factor $R'$. Thus the assertion includes shifts in $M$, not only shifts of the scalar factor. Finally the natural comparisons, restriction equations, field projection equality and point projection equality established above are precisely the fields required by [def-sfb-field-action-coefficient-transport-data]. They supply that coefficient datum, with no exactness assertion about $S_T$.
